evidence: Paper Invest Basic is officially $0/month free forever and includes API & MCP access; its developer page says a free API key can be obtained with no credit card.

Paper's official developer materials explicitly target trading-bot and algorithmic/API use, and document GET /v1/market-data/quote/{symbol} as a real-time NBBO quote with bid/ask sizes plus a separate GET /v1/market-data/trade/{symbol} endpoint.

Paper's official MCP server README describes paper.quote(symbol) as a real-time NBBO quote and proxies the official Paper market-data API; scheduler/API callability is technically plausible using a dedicated API key/JWT.

The REST quote and REST trade objects each expose a timestamp field, creating a technically valid two-endpoint path for quote/trade freshness checks, but public docs do not explicitly define those values as independent upstream quote-event and trade-event timestamps rather than service timestamps. Same-run RTH live validation remains mandatory.

The dedicated WebSocket documentation requires PRO and wins over broader marketing wording that says free quote streaming. Strict G9 must therefore rely only on the documented Basic REST/API path unless Paper changes the dedicated entitlement page.

Paper's free/no-credit-card/API-and-bot wording materially supports zero-dollar programmatic use, but no primary-source Paper market-data license/terms statement found so far explicitly says upstream CTA/UTP/SIP or equivalent exchange/vendor non-display fees are absorbed for this Basic REST entitlement.

Public official docs repeatedly call the quote NBBO, but no primary-source Paper document found so far identifies CTA/UTP SIP or a named licensed consolidated redistributor as the lineage. Strict G9-A therefore remains unproven.

Accordingly, C is narrowed to one unresolved legal/entitlement question: whether the Basic REST market-data license explicitly covers automated/non-display consolidated NBBO use with no separate exchange/vendor fee or other monetary/account condition.

UTP's current Detailed Usage Reporting Codes (updated 2024-10; fees as of 2025) define UTP1APIS = Real-Time Nonprofessional Uncontrolled Recipient at $1/month billable to the Vendor, and UTP Data Policies expressly list API as an Uncontrolled Product.

This means Paper's Basic $0/free-forever API can be economically compatible with strict G9-C if Paper lawfully classifies the exact single-user automated API entitlement under UTP1APIS or an equivalent approved category and absorbs the vendor assessment. XRAY must not assume that classification.
exact_provider_question: For the Basic/free REST API, please confirm (1) the bid/ask returned by GET /v1/market-data/quote/{symbol} are the live consolidated U.S. National Best Bid and Offer for Nasdaq-listed securities sourced from the UTP SIP (UQDF/UTDF) or identify the licensed consolidated redistributor that supplies them; (2) quote.timestamp is the upstream quote-event time and GET /v1/market-data/trade/{symbol}.timestamp is independently the upstream trade-event time; and (3) a single nonprofessional end user using the Basic REST API programmatically/through third-party automation is lawfully covered under UTP1APIS or an equivalent approved nonprofessional uncontrolled classification, with any UTP/exchange/vendor assessment absorbed by Paper so the user owes $0 permanently and has no subscription, funding, balance, activity, account-maintenance, or per-query condition.
reopen_condition: Primary-source Paper confirmation of exact lineage + UTP1APIS/equivalent approved classification and vendor fee absorption + upstream event timestamp semantics; then configure a dedicated market-data credential and require same-run RTH freshness/skew probe.
